content.text: When you stretch a rubber band or compress a spring, you store energy in it. This stored energy is called elastic potential energy. It's released when the object returns to its original shape, which is why stretched elastic bands can fly across the room!

Elastic potential energy is stored when an object is stretched or compressed. The equation EPE = 1/2 ke^2 only applies when the elastic limit has not been exceeded (i.e. the material still obeys Hooke's Law).

— k = 2 x EPE / e² = 2 x 18 / 0.3² = 36 / 0.09 = 400 N/m (calculation)
— EPE = 0.5 x 400 x 0.08² = 0.64 J. v = sqrt(2 x EPE / m) = sqrt(2 x 0.64 / 0.02) = sqrt(64) = 8 m/s (calculation)
— EPE = 0.5 x 500 x 0.2² = 0.5 x 500 x 0.04 = 10 J (calculation)

As the bow is drawn further, the extension e increases. Since EPE = 0.5ke², the energy stored is proportional to the square of the extension. Each additional centimetre of draw adds more energy than the last because the restoring force is also increasing (F = ke). The increasing force is why it feels harder to pull, yet this greater force over additional distance means even more work is done, storing more energy.
